title: Simple yet Effective Diffusion-based Graph Data Augmentation via Complementary Diffusion Transfer

problem.claim: Graph imperfections such as noise and incompleteness can hinder GNN effectiveness.

gap.claim: Existing diffusion-based graph data augmentation approaches may discard valuable propagated information through hard masking or truncation.

contributions.claim: CoDiT constructs two complementary diffusion views and compensates for missing diffusion signals through cross-view transfer.
CoDiT decomposes a truncated diffusion matrix into disjoint complementary components and uses view-specific masked propagation with cross-view information transfer.
CoDiT fuses original and transferred representations through interpolation and trains a shared classifier with supervised and consistency-regularization losses.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe CoDiT as a novel approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on five real-world datasets.
The authors report that CoDiT outperforms thirteen competitive baselines.
The authors characterize CoDiT as lightweight because it adds no generative modules while maintaining high representation quality.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are effective tools for modeling relational data and supporting downstream tasks.
Graph imperfections hinder GNN robustness, while existing diffusion-based augmentation can discard propagated information.
CoDiT uses complementary diffusion views, cross-view transfer, interpolation-based fusion, and a hybrid training objective.
Experiments on five real-world datasets are reported to show superiority over thirteen baselines.
